messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Threat
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Triggers → Threat
  - Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals → Threat
  - Threat → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Threat → Negative Appraisals
  - Threat → Triggers
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Negative Appraisals
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Triggers

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

The violence that scarred Kwame began not with shouts, but with sensory precision. When his father’s hand closed around his wrist, the rough weave of the man’s work glove against Kwame’s skin left an indelible tactile imprint. The room would always drop to a biting chill, the kind that seeped through thin shirts and settled in the bones, while the steady, heavy tread of footsteps on the stairwell served as a relentless countdown. As a child, Kwame learned to map survival to those exact coordinates. Now, at twenty-seven, those memories have calcified into a rigid internal architecture. He has come to believe he is permanently changed for the worse, his character fractured beyond repair. He views his own physiology as a traitor, a body that keeps reacting as if he is still in danger even when he is safe. Worse, he feels he has lost his connection to his community and culture, drifting through life while his family and elders remain anchored in traditions he can no longer participate in. This fractured worldview dictates how Kwame navigates his shifts as a rideshare driver. When he settles into his cab, the moment his palm meets the rough synthetic texture of the steering wheel, a draft of cold air hits his neck, and he hears the muffled rhythm of footsteps on the pavement, those exact sensory markers force him to immediately turn up the static-laced radio to drown out the memory and slide a sedative across his lips. The triggers do not just startle him; they snap his nervous system into a state of relentless watchfulness, locking him in hyperarousal where every tailing vehicle and sudden brake feels like an imminent strike. His conviction that he is permanently damaged and that he has lost his community fuels a deep suspicion that safety is a lie, pushing him to take reckless risks on the highway, merging too fast and braking too late, just to assert a fragile sense of control. The exhaustion from living in this perpetual state of threat narrows his perceptual field, so that minor environmental shifts instantly register as coordinates of past violence, sharpening the sensitivity of his original triggers. The constant vigilance and dangerous driving confirm his deepest fears; every near-miss and every flinch against the glass reinforces his conviction that he is irrevocably broken and that he can no longer trust his own capacity to navigate the world safely. Because he believes he is permanently damaged and that his body is an enemy, he pulls away from any attempt at emotional closeness, shutting down when women in his life try to understand him. The relentless scanning and compulsion to prove his alertness leave him completely drained, which in turn pushes him to dissociate behind the wheel with pills and to avoid intimacy entirely. The longer he avoids intimacy and masks his reactions with distraction and chemical dampening, the more certain he becomes that he has severed his ties to his community and culture, alienating the few family members who still reach out. His reliance on distraction and substances creates a volatile baseline; when the fog inevitably lifts between doses, the raw texture of the gear shift, the sudden drop in cabin temperature, and the sound of approaching footsteps hit him with amplified, unfiltered intensity. The cycle tightens. He knows he is driving recklessly to outrun his own nervous system, but he cannot stop. What finally brought him to this intake was a moment where a passenger’s casual touch on his shoulder during exit triggered a full-body panic response, causing him to slam on the brakes in the middle of a busy intersection. He is terrified that he will lose his license, lose his livelihood, or worse, lose the last fragile grip on a life that now feels entirely foreign. He came to the clinic hoping someone could help him quiet the body that refuses to stand down, and perhaps, against all his convictions, learn to trust that the past is no longer standing behind him.
